facts.fact: L'Umbracle is a sculpture garden and landscaped walk in Valencia's City of Arts and Sciences, planted with species native to Valencia.
facts.quote: L'Umbracle (Valencian: [lumˈbɾakle]), part of the City of Arts and Sciences complex in Valencia, Spain, is a sculpture garden and landscaped walk with plant species indigenous to Valencia (such as rockrose, lentisca, rosemary, honeysuckle, bougainvillea and palm trees).

facts.fact: Inside it is the Walk of the Sculptures, an outdoor gallery of works by contemporary artists.
facts.quote: It harbors in its interior The Walk of the Sculptures, an outdoor art gallery with sculptures from contemporary artists (Miquel of Navarre, Francesc Abbot, Yoko Ono and others).

facts.fact: Santiago Calatrava designed it as an entrance on the complex's southwestern edge and as a cover over its car park; it was completed in 2001.
facts.quote: It was designed by Santiago Calatrava as an entrance along the southwestern edge to the City of Arts and Sciences and as a cover over its car park. L'Umbracle was completed in 2001.

facts.fact: It is 320 metres long and 60 metres wide, with 55 fixed and 54 floating arches 18 metres high.
facts.quote: It is 320 metres (1,050 ft) long and 60 metres (200 ft) wide, located on the southern side of the complex. It has 55 fixed arches and 54 floating arches that stand 18 metres (59 ft) high.

facts.fact: The arches are parabolic.
facts.quote: The arches are parabolic.

facts.fact: The plants were chosen to change colour with the seasons; the garden includes 99 palm trees and 62 bitter orange trees.
facts.quote: The plants in the garden were carefully picked to change colour with the seasons. The garden consists of 99 palm trees, 78 small palm trees, and 62 bitter orange trees.

facts.fact: In Calatrava's revised plan, L'Umbracle was placed parallel to the complex's long axis, alongside the science museum, raised promenades and reflecting pools.
facts.quote: Parallel to the axis were placed the science museum, L'Umbracle, raised promenades and reflecting pools.

facts.fact: Trencadís ceramic mosaic, a traditional Valencian finish, covers concrete surfaces across the complex.
facts.quote: Another unifying element was the use of the city’s traditional heritage, viz., the use of ceramic mosaic tiles known as “trencadis”, which was widely used as the exterior layer over the concrete surfaces of many of the buildings/structures and elements of the promenade throughout the complex.

facts.fact: The Steiner House in Vienna is considered one of Adolf Loos's major works.
facts.quote: Steiner House is a building in Vienna, Austria. It is considered one of the major works of architect Adolf Loos.

facts.fact: Loos designed and built it in 1910, early in his career, and it quickly became a worldwide example of rationalist architecture.
facts.quote: Loos was still starting his career in 1910 when he designed and constructed the Steiner house in Vienna, Austria. This design was much better accepted than Loos' earlier works and quickly became a worldwide example of rationalist architecture.

facts.fact: Loos made a classical three-part facade by recessing the space between the two wings of the house all the way to the roof.
facts.quote: In the Steiner house, Loos uses his volumes to create a classical tripartite façade. He does this by creating a recess between the two wings of the house that continues straight to the roof.

facts.fact: The living area sits slightly above ground level, apart from the bedrooms and the painting studio on the first floor.
facts.quote: The Steiner house features a living area that is raised slightly above the ground level and separated from more private areas of the house such as bedrooms and painting studio, which was located on the first floor.

facts.fact: Service spaces were put in the basement and attic, apart from the main rooms.
facts.quote: The served space in this house is neatly separated from the serving space by placing the serving space in the basement and attic.

facts.fact: The roughcast brick walls have a stucco skin, giving a smooth, unornamented white surface.
facts.quote: The stucco façades have another benefit: they create a smooth, unornamented, and white surface.

facts.fact: Allowed only one floor above street level, Loos gave the street side a quarter-round roof that hides the two upper floors facing the garden.
facts.quote: This led him to create a one quarter round roof that is facing the street. This roof flattens out the apex and makes the two additional floors that look out onto the garden impossible to see from the street.

facts.fact: Aschanska Villa in Umeå was designed by Ragnar Östberg and completed in 1906 for Colonel Wilhelm Aschan, head of the Norrland dragoon regiment.
facts.quote: The villa was designed by the architect Ragnar Östberg and it was completed in 1906 for Colonel Wilhelm Aschan who led the Norrlands dragonregemente.

facts.fact: Today the building is a restaurant.
facts.quote: Today the building is a restaurant.

facts.fact: The wooden villa is in the National Romantic style, like Östberg's Scharinska Villa built nearby the year before.
facts.quote: The wooden villa is designed in the National Romantic style similar to Scharinska Villa which had been built locally by the same architect the year before.

facts.fact: It stands on a stone foundation and plinth.
facts.quote: The villa stands on a stone foundation and plinth.

facts.fact: The building has been listed since the 1980s.
facts.quote: The building has been listed since the 1980s.

facts.fact: Östberg, best known for Stockholm City Hall, became the most famous architect of Sweden's national romanticist movement.
facts.quote: Östberg became the most famous architect within the so-called "national romanticist" movement in Sweden.

facts.fact: The Banovina Palace in Novi Sad is a complex of two buildings: the larger Banovina houses the Government of Vojvodina and the smaller Banski dvor its Assembly.
facts.quote: The larger Banovina serves as the seat of the Government of Vojvodina, while the smaller Banski dvor serves as the seat of the Assembly of Vojvodina.

facts.fact: Designed by Dragiša Brašovan, the buildings were built between 1936 and 1940 in modernist style with art deco and stripped classicism elements, as the seat of the Danube Banovina.
facts.quote: The buildings, designed by Dragiša Brašovan, were constructed between 1936 and 1940 in modernist style (with art deco and stripped classicism elements) as the administrative seat of the Danube Banovina.

facts.fact: Brašovan was given the project even though his entry had done poorly in the 1930 national competition.
facts.quote: Due to a series of circumstances, Dragiša Brašovan was ultimately entrusted creation and realization of a new project, despite the fact that his work fared rather poorly in the competition.

facts.fact: During construction it was decided to face the building with marble and other stone instead of the planned clinker brick.
facts.quote: The building would cover its façade with marble and other stones, instead of the previously planned clinker bricks.

facts.fact: The Banovina building has an elongated horseshoe plan, with a semicircular west end and a square tower at the east end.
facts.quote: The Banovina building has a closed elongated horseshoe-shaped base. The semi-circular part of the building is located on the western side, while on the eastern side, there is a tower with a square base.

facts.fact: It is 180 metres long and about 20 metres high, with a 42-metre tower, clad in white Brač marble outside and Carrara marble inside.
facts.quote: It is 180 meters long, 44 meters wide, and around 20 meters high (except for the tower, which is 42 meters high). It is covered with white Brač island marble from the Pučišća quarry, while the interior is covered with Carrara marble.

facts.fact: Because it looks like a large ship with a mast, the Banovina is also called the White Cruiser.
facts.quote: Due to the buildings design resembling a large ship with a sail mast, the Banovina was also called the White Cruiser.

facts.fact: It has 569 rooms, mostly offices along the outer facade, reached by wide corridors facing four inner courtyards.
facts.quote: Most of the rooms are office spaces, arranged continuously along the external façade, accessible with wide corridors oriented towards the four inner courtyards.

facts.fact: Copenhagen City Hall houses the city council and the Lord Mayor's office.
facts.quote: It houses the headquarters of the Copenhagen City Council as well as the office of the Lord mayor of the Copenhagen Municipality.

facts.fact: The current building, the city's sixth city hall, was designed by Martin Nyrop and built between 1892 and 1905.
facts.quote: The sixth incarnation of the Copenhagen City Hall, the current building in National Romantic Renaissance Revial style was designed by the Danish architect Martin Nyrop and constructed between 1892 and 1905.

facts.fact: Nyrop won the commission through an architectural competition.
facts.quote: After an architectural competition, the architect Martin Nyrop won the assignment of constructing the sixth and current city hall.

facts.fact: It is in the National Romantic style, inspired by the City Hall of Siena in Italy.
facts.quote: Martin Nyrop's city hall is designed in the National Romantic style but with inspiration from the City Hall of Siena, Italy.

facts.fact: Its slim clock tower, 105.6 metres tall, is one of the tallest buildings in low-rise Copenhagen.
facts.quote: The latter is, at 105.6 metres, one of the tallest buildings in the generally low city of Copenhagen.

facts.fact: Two long wings are joined by three cross buildings, with the covered Main Hall and the open-air City Hall Garden between them.
facts.quote: The City Hall building consists of two longitudinal wings along Vester Voldgade and H.C. Andersens Boulevard respectively. They are connected by three transverse buildings. Between the three transverse buildings are the covered Main Hall and the open-air City Hall Garden.

facts.fact: The square in front was modelled on Siena's shell-shaped Piazza del Campo.
facts.quote: The design of the city hall was greatly inspired by the Palazzo Pubblico in Siena, Italy, and the design of the square was accordingly modeled on the shell-shaped Piazza del Campo outside that building.

facts.fact: Dia Beacon is the museum for the Dia Art Foundation's collection of art from the 1960s to today; it opened in 2003 near the Hudson River in Beacon, New York.
facts.quote: Dia Beacon is the museum for the Dia Art Foundation's collection of art from the 1960s to the present and is one of the 12 locations and sites they manage. The museum, which opened in 2003, is situated near the banks of the Hudson River in Beacon, New York.

facts.fact: Its building is a former Nabisco box-printing plant, renovated by Dia with artist Robert Irwin and architects Alan Koch, Lyn Rice, Galia Solomonoff and Linda Taalman, then of OpenOffice.
facts.quote: Dia Beacon's facility, the Riggio Galleries, is a former Nabisco box-printing facility that was renovated by Dia with artist Robert Irwin and architects Alan Koch, Lyn Rice, Galia Solomonoff, and Linda Taalman, then of OpenOffice.

facts.fact: With 240,000 square feet, it is one of the largest exhibition spaces for modern and contemporary art in the United States.
facts.quote: With 240,000 square feet (22,000 m2), it is one of the largest exhibition spaces in the country for modern and contemporary art.

facts.fact: Dia pioneered converting industrial buildings to show contemporary art, a practice now widely adopted by museums and galleries.
facts.quote: Dia pioneered the conversion of industrial buildings for the installation of contemporary art, a practice and aesthetic now widely adopted by museums and galleries internationally.

facts.fact: The printing plant was built by Nabisco in 1929.
facts.quote: Dia's most recent conversion, its museum in Beacon, is located in a former printing plant built in 1929 by Nabisco (National Biscuit Company).

facts.fact: Each gallery was designed specifically for the art it holds.
facts.quote: In keeping with Dia's history of single-artist, site-related presentations, each gallery was designed specifically for the art it contains.

facts.fact: More than 34,000 square feet of skylights give the galleries reflected north light.
facts.quote: The ideal viewing conditions created by reflected north light from more than 34,000 square feet (3,200 m2) of skylights are especially evident in the galleries devoted to the paintings of On Kawara, Agnes Martin, Blinky Palermo, and Robert Ryman.

facts.fact: Irwin designed the entrance court and parking lot with a grove of flowering fruit trees, and a formal garden.
facts.quote: The grounds include an entrance court and parking lot with a grove of flowering fruit trees and a formal garden, both of which were designed by Irwin.

facts.fact: The museum was in a three-storey building across from Bellevue Square, opened in 2001 and designed by Steven Holl.
facts.quote: The museum was located across from Bellevue Square in a three-story building opened in 2001 and designed by architect Steven Holl.

facts.fact: Many residents see the building as part of downtown Bellevue's change from suburban strip malls to a city with cultural attractions.
facts.quote: It is seen by many residents of Bellevue as playing a role in the transformation of the downtown from series of suburban strip malls to a sophisticated city with a variety of cultural attractions.

facts.fact: After a $3 million fundraising campaign and extensive interior remodelling, the museum reopened in 2005.
facts.quote: After a successful $3 million fundraising campaign and extensive interior remodeling, the museum re-opened on June 18, 2005, with a revised mission focused on art, craft and design and with an emphasis on Northwest artists.

facts.fact: Unlike conventional art museums, it had no permanent collection.
facts.quote: In contrast to conventional art museums, Bellevue Arts Museum has no permanent collection.

facts.fact: The museum space closed on 4 September 2024 amid financial problems.
facts.quote: A nonprofit organization established in 1975, the Bellevue Arts Museum (BAM) provided rotating arts exhibitions to the public until the closure of its museum space on September 4, 2024, amid financial issues.

facts.fact: In October 2025 the museum said it would sell the building and land to the KidsQuest Children's Museum.
facts.quote: In October 2025, the museum announced that it would sell the building and land to the KidsQuest Children's Museum, a Bellevue-based children's museum that focuses on STEM education.

facts.fact: 66 Old Church Street, also called Levy House, is a house in Chelsea, London.
facts.quote: 66 Old Church Street, also known as Levy House, is a house on Old Church Street in Chelsea, London.

facts.fact: Walter Gropius and Maxwell Fry designed it in 1935–36 for the politician and playwright Benn Levy.
facts.quote: It was designed by Walter Gropius and Maxwell Fry between 1935 and 1936 for the politician and playwright Benn Levy.

facts.fact: It was built as part of a joint development with Cohen House.
facts.quote: Levy House is part of a joint development with Cohen House.

facts.fact: It was listed at Grade II in 1970.
facts.quote: It was listed at Grade II on the National Heritage List for England in 1970.

facts.fact: Carew Tower is a 49-storey, 574-foot Art Deco skyscraper in downtown Cincinnati, the city's tallest from 1930 until 2011.
facts.quote: Carew Tower is a 49-story, 574-foot (175 m) Art Deco skyscraper in downtown Cincinnati, Ohio. The second-tallest building in the city, it was Cincinnati's tallest from 1930 until 2011, when it was surpassed by Great American Tower at Queen City Square.

facts.fact: Developer John J. Emery wanted a mixed-use "city within a city" with offices, shops, a hotel and a parking garage.
facts.quote: The Carew Tower was developed by industrialist John J. Emery, who sought to create a mixed-use "city within a city" with an office and retail tower, a hotel, and a parking garage.

facts.fact: Walter W. Ahlschlager was the principal architect, with Delano & Aldrich as associate architect.
facts.quote: Walter W. Ahlschlager served as the complex's principal architect, with Delano & Aldrich as an associate architect.

facts.fact: Many of Ahlschlager's proposals were dropped; the final design was prepared by Delano & Aldrich.
facts.quote: Many of his proposals did not make it into the final design, which was prepared by Delano & Aldrich and influenced by its earlier Wall and Hanover Building.

facts.fact: Work went on through the start of the Great Depression; the complex was complete by early 1931 at a cost of $33 million.
facts.quote: Announced shortly before the onset of the Great Depression in 1929, work on the project continued despite poor economic conditions. The office and retail tower topped out in July 1930, and the entire complex was complete by early 1931 at a cost of $33 million ($636 million in 2025).

facts.fact: The tower held offices on most floors, a retail arcade on the lower levels and an observation deck on top.
facts.quote: Upon its completion in 1930, the tallest of the complex's three towers housed commercial offices on the majority of floors, a retail arcade on the lower levels, and an observation deck on the top floor.

facts.fact: Its 15,000-ton steel frame went up in 61 days, a world record for speed.
facts.quote: With 15,000 tons of steel raised over 61 days, the speed at which the framework had been completed set a world record.

facts.fact: It was designated a National Historic Landmark in 1994; the National Park Service called it one of the finest examples of skyscraper modernism in America.
facts.quote: It was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1982 and was designated a National Historic Landmark in 1994, with the National Park Service describing it as "one of the finest examples of skyscraper modernism in America" and "the most complete statement of the 1920s' Jazz Age".

facts.fact: Vestersøhus was built from 1935 to 1939 by Kay Fisker and C. F. Møller.
facts.quote: Vestersøhus was built from 1935 to 1939 by Fisker and C. F. Møller.

facts.fact: It at once became the Danish model for apartment blocks with balconies and bay windows.
facts.quote: It instantly became a model in Denmark for the balcony and bay window blocks of the time.

facts.fact: The Copenhagen apartment block has remained a major influence on Danish housing architecture.
facts.quote: Their buildings also include the apartment blocks 2 Vodroffsvej (1930) and Vestersøhus (1935–1939) in Copenhagen, the latter of which has remained a major influence on Danish housing architecture.

facts.fact: Pavel Janák's Adria Palace of 1925 is an unusually late example of sculpture built into architecture.
facts.quote: His 1925 Palace Adria is an unusually late example of integrated sculpture.

facts.fact: Janák later designed the neighbouring Škoda Palace, perhaps because he had designed the Adria Palace next door.
facts.quote: In the end, Pavel Janák, a professor of Prague's Academy of Arts, Architecture and Design was entrusted with the task, perhaps because he had also authored the neighbouring facility, the Adria Palace.

facts.fact: Langham House Close on Ham Common, London, is a group of three Grade II* listed buildings designed in 1955 by James Gowan and James Stirling.
facts.quote: Langham House Close on Ham Common in Ham in the London Borough of Richmond upon Thames is a development of three Grade II* listed buildings designed in 1955 by the British architects James Gowan and James Stirling.

facts.fact: Influenced by Le Corbusier, it was the pair's first major project together and made their name as leaders of Brutalism; it was built in 1957–58.
facts.quote: The Le Corbusier-influenced buildings were the architects' first major project working together and cemented their reputation as leaders amongst the Brutalist movement. The development was constructed during 1957–58 for Manousso Group.

facts.fact: Nikolaus Pevsner called it a landmark of the late-1950s English reaction against all-glass facades and thin, precise detailing.
facts.quote: Nikolaus Pevsner writes that it was "a landmark in the emerging style of the late 1950s in England, in reaction against all-glass facades and thin, precise detailing".

facts.fact: It has three flat-roofed blocks: a three-storey block of 18 flats by Stirling and two two-storey blocks of six flats by Gowan.
facts.quote: The development comprises three flat-roofed blocks, one three-storey block of 18 flats designed by Stirling and two, two-storey blocks of six flats designed by Gowan, the two architects following common themes yet expressing individual features.

facts.fact: The buildings use second-hand stock brick, echoing old Langham House, with in-situ shuttered concrete left exposed outside and inside.
facts.quote: Constructed of second-hand stock brick reflecting the construction of old Langham House, the buildings use in-situ shuttered concrete, blatantly exposed on exterior and repeated in interior surfaces.

facts.fact: Each flat has a central fireplace unit set in exposed brick with concrete lintels and shelves, echoing the exterior on a smaller scale.
facts.quote: The flats themselves share common features. Each has a central fireplace with back boiler and linen cupboard set in exposed stock brick with concrete lintels and shelves repeating the exterior surface themes on a smaller scale.

facts.fact: Critic Ian Nairn called it the first building in a new tough style.
facts.quote: In 1966 architectural critic Ian Nairn described the development as the first building in a new tough style which was as much a reaction against well-meaning vacuity as the Angry plays and novels.

facts.fact: It was listed Grade II in 1998 and raised to Grade II* in 2006.
facts.quote: Langham House Close was listed Grade II in 1998 and reclassified Grade II* in 2006 following pressure from the Twentieth Century Society.

facts.fact: Dům Radost ("House of Joy") is a functionalist building in Prague's Žižkov district, built between 1932 and 1934.
facts.quote: Dům Radost (translated from Czech: House of Joy) is a functionalist building in Prague, Czech Republic. It is located next to Winston Churchill square in Žižkov district. It was built between 1932 and 1934.

facts.fact: The 52-metre, 13-floor building has a cruciform plan inspired by Le Corbusier and was once the tallest office building in the country.
facts.quote: This 52-metre-high (171 ft) building with 13 floors and a cruciform floor plan inspired by French architect Le Corbusier was once the tallest office building in the country.

facts.fact: It now holds offices, apartments, a theatre, a cinema, a cafe and, since 2019, an observatory.
facts.quote: The complex serves as offices, apartments, theater, cinema, cafe and observatory since 2019.

facts.fact: It has been a cultural monument of the Czech Republic since 1964.
facts.quote: Since 1964, it is a cultural monument of the Czech Republic.

facts.fact: It was historically known as the House of Trade Unions or the General Pension Administration Palace.
facts.quote: The building is historically known as Dům odborových svazů (translated as House of Trade Unions) or palác Všeobecného penzijního ústavu (translated as General Pension Administration Palace).

facts.fact: Its facade earned it the nickname "Tile House".
facts.quote: Sometimes, it is also called as kachlíkárna (badly translated as Tile Factory, better as Tile House) due to its facade.

facts.fact: Case Study House No. 1 was designed by J. R. Davidson for the Case Study Houses program.
facts.quote: It was designed by JR Davidson as part of the Case Study Houses program.

facts.fact: The single-storey house, completed in 1948, is a wood frame on a concrete foundation, with glass, concrete block and plywood throughout.
facts.quote: The single-story house was completed in 1948 and consists of a wood frame on a concrete foundation, with glass, concrete blocks, and plywood used throughout.

facts.fact: It stands out for its room layouts, built-in storage and furniture, and guest quarters set apart from the rest of the house.
facts.quote: Designed by JR Davidson as part of the Case Study Houses program, Case Study House No. 1 is distinctive for its room layouts, use of built-in storage and furniture, and the inclusion of guest quarters separate from the rest of the house.

facts.fact: High walls face the street, while full-height glass doors and windows face the garden and pool at the back.
facts.quote: The house's facade consists largely of high walls facing the street and full-height glass doors and windows facing the garden and pool in the rear.

facts.fact: The program, which ran until 1966, sought inexpensive, efficient model homes to meet postwar housing demand in the United States.
facts.quote: The program, which ran until 1966, sought to develop inexpensive and efficient model homes to meet housing demand in the postwar United States.

facts.fact: Davidson designed the house for an imagined working couple with a teenage daughter and a visiting mother-in-law.
facts.quote: Davidson sought to design the house for a theoretical "Mr. and Mrs. X", a working couple with a teenage daughter and occasional visits from a mother-in-law.

facts.fact: Despite its number, it was not the first Case Study house built: that was Davidson's No. 11, finished in 1946.
facts.quote: Despite its number, House 1 was not the first house constructed; that distinction belongs to Case Study House No. 11, also designed by Davidson and finished in 1946.

facts.fact: It was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 2013, with nine other Case Study houses.
facts.quote: House 1, along with nine of the other remaining Case Study houses, were added to the National Register of Historic Places in 2013.

facts.fact: The Fine Arts Center, now the Randolph W. Bromery Center for the Arts, at UMass Amherst holds a concert hall and a contemporary art gallery.
facts.quote: The Randolph W. Bromery Center for the Arts at the University of Massachusetts Amherst, formerly and commonly known as the Fine Arts Center, is an arts center located just north of downtown Amherst, Massachusetts, and contains a concert hall and a contemporary art gallery.

facts.fact: The building is a 646-foot-long bridge of studio space raised 30 feet off the ground, forming a gateway to the campus.
facts.quote: The building is a 646-foot-long bridge of studio art space, raised up 30 feet from the ground creating a monumental gateway for a campus.

facts.fact: In the late 1960s Kevin Roche and John Dinkeloo were asked to design first-class art, music and theatre spaces for the children of Massachusetts' working families.
facts.quote: In the late 1960s, Kevin Roche and John Dinkeloo were asked to design first-class art, music, and theater spaces for the sons and daughters of working men and women of Massachusetts.

facts.fact: It was built between 1972 and 1974 and opened on 10 October 1975.
facts.quote: The structure was constructed between 1972 and 1974 and opened October 10, 1975.

facts.fact: The Brutalist poured-concrete structure is 646 feet long and 66 feet high and is reflected in the nearby pond.
facts.quote: The Bromery Center for the Arts is a 646-foot-long and 66 foot-high, Brutalist, poured stereo metric concrete, partially bridge-like structure, which are reflected in the nearby pond.

facts.fact: Its 2,000-seat performance hall was the campus's main venue until the Mullins Center opened in 1993.
facts.quote: The 2000-seat performance hall within the Fine Arts building was the main venue on the campus before the Mullins Center was opened in 1993.

facts.fact: The Palace of Assembly in Chandigarh houses the Punjab and Haryana Legislative Assemblies and was designed by Le Corbusier.
facts.quote: The Palace of Assembly is a building in Chandigarh, India which houses the Punjab Legislative Assembly and the Haryana Legislative Assembly. It was designed by  modernist architect Le Corbusier.

facts.fact: It is part of the Chandigarh Capitol Complex, with the Secretariat and the High Court.
facts.quote: It is part of the Chandigarh Capitol Complex, which includes the Legislative Assembly, Secretariat and High Court.

facts.fact: It has a circular assembly chamber, a forum for conversation and stair-free circulation.
facts.quote: The Palace of Assembly features a circular assembly chamber, a forum for conversation and transactions, and stair-free circulation.

facts.fact: It became part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2016.
facts.quote: The building was designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2016.

facts.fact: Construction ran from 1951 to 1962, and the building was inaugurated on 15 April 1964.
facts.quote: Construction of the Palace of Assembly began in 1951 and ended 11 years later in 1962. The building was inaugurated on 15 April 1964.

facts.fact: Its enamelled ceremonial door, nearly 2.3 m², was airlifted from Paris.
facts.quote: The nearly 2.3 m2 (25 ft2) door, with its enamelled panels, was airlifted from Paris.

facts.fact: High ceilings and narrow columns make the space feel large, and ramps replace stairs between levels.
facts.quote: High ceilings and narrow columns make the space feel expansive, and ramps replace stairs to provide fluid transitions between levels.

facts.fact: The circular General Assembly chamber sits off-centre in the building.
facts.quote: The General Assembly itself is circular – a literal interpretation of Le Corbusier's belief – and is off-centre within the space, challenging neoclassical architecture's focus on organization.

facts.fact: The National Congress Palace in Brasília is the meeting place of Brazil's national legislature; like most of the city's government buildings, it was designed by Oscar Niemeyer in the Modernist style.
facts.quote: As with most of the city's government buildings, the National Congress building was designed by Oscar Niemeyer in the Modernist style.

facts.fact: It stands in the middle of the Monumental Axis, with a large lawn in front and the Three Powers Plaza behind.
facts.quote: The building is located in the middle of the Monumental Axis, the main street of Brasília. In front of it there is a large lawn where demonstrations take place.

facts.fact: Lúcio Costa's plan placed the legislative palace at the vertex of the triangular Three Powers Plaza.
facts.quote: In item 9 of the justification report, Costa defined the Praça dos Três Poderes as a triangle in which each of the three branches of government would occupy one corner, with the legislative palace located at the vertex.

facts.fact: Niemeyer sent sketches of the curved forms to engineer Joaquim Cardozo, who calculated how the concrete could hold them; the Chamber's dome had to look as if it simply rested on the slab.
facts.quote: Niemeyer produced sketches of the design and sent the curved forms to the engineer, whose task was to perform the mathematical calculations needed for the concrete structure to support the smooth shapes. The goal was to create two distinct domes, with an additional challenge for the dome of the Chamber of Deputies, which had to appear as if it were simply resting on the slab.

facts.fact: The Chamber of Deputies' dome is 10 metres high, like the Senate dome, but 62 metres across.
facts.quote: Structurally, it posed a greater challenge for Joaquim Cardozo: it has the same height as the Senate dome (10 metres) but a diameter of 62 metres.

facts.fact: The complex includes two 28-storey office towers.
facts.quote: The complex includes two office towers with 28 floors each.

facts.fact: The building was inaugurated on 21 April 1960, the same day as the city.
facts.quote: The Congress was inaugurated in Brasília on 21 April 1960, on the same day the city itself was inaugurated.

facts.fact: It has been part of Brasília's UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1987.
facts.quote: The building has also been a UNESCO World Heritage Site, as part of Brasília's original urban buildings, since 1987.

facts.fact: Casa Milà was Gaudí's last private residence, built between 1906 and 1912.
facts.quote: It was the last private residence designed by architect Antoni Gaudí and was built between 1906 and 1912.

facts.fact: Its structural innovations include a self-supporting stone facade, a free-plan floor, an underground garage and the roof terrace.
facts.quote: Several structural innovations include a self-supporting stone façade, and a free-plan floor, underground garage and the spectacular terrace on the roof.

facts.fact: Gaudí designed the house as a constant curve, inside and out, using ruled geometry and forms from nature.
facts.quote: He designed the house as a constant curve, both outside and inside, incorporating ruled geometry and naturalistic elements.

facts.fact: Two courtyards bring light into the building's nine storeys.
facts.quote: Casa Milà consists of two buildings, which are structured around two courtyards that provide light to the nine stories: basement, ground floor, mezzanine, main (or noble) floor, four upper floors, and an attic.

facts.fact: Curved iron beams around each floor tie the facade to the structure, so there are no load-bearing walls and inner walls can be moved freely.
facts.quote: This construction system allows, on one hand, large openings in the facade which give light to the homes, and on the other, free structuring of the different levels, so that internal walls can be added and demolished without affecting the stability of the building.

facts.fact: The roof's skylights, stair exits, fans and chimneys are working parts that are also sculptures.
facts.quote: All of these elements, constructed out of brick covered with lime, broken marble, or glass have a specific architectural function but are also real sculptures integrated into the building.

facts.fact: The facade is made of large limestone blocks from the Garraf Massif and the Villefranche quarry.
facts.quote: The facade is composed of large blocks of limestone from the Garraf Massif on the first floor and from the Villefranche quarry for the higher levels.

facts.fact: It was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1984.
facts.quote: In 1984, it was declared a World Heritage Site by UNESCO.

facts.fact: Michael Arad won the competition to design the memorial in 2004.
facts.quote: He won the competition to design the memorial in 2004.

facts.fact: Arad's design, Reflecting Absence, made with landscape architect Peter Walker, was chosen from 5,201 entries from 63 countries.
facts.quote: In January 2004, Reflecting Absence, by architect Michael Arad of Handel Architects and landscape architect Peter Walker, was selected from 5,201 entries from 63 countries as the winner of the LMDC's design competition.

facts.fact: Two one-acre pools with the largest man-made waterfalls in the United States fill the footprints of the Twin Towers, marking the loss of life and the void left by the attacks.
facts.quote: Two 1-acre (4,000 m2) pools with the largest man-made waterfalls in the United States comprise the footprints of the Twin Towers, symbolizing the loss of life and the physical void left by the attacks.

facts.fact: The waterfalls are meant to mute the sounds of the city and make the site a place for contemplation.
facts.quote: The waterfalls are intended to mute the sounds of the city, making the site a contemplative sanctuary.

facts.fact: More than 400 swamp white oaks fill the memorial plaza.
facts.quote: More than 400 swamp white oak trees fill the Memorial plaza, enhancing the site's reflective nature.

facts.fact: The trees stand in rows and form informal clusters, clearings and groves; the park is at street level above the Memorial Museum.
facts.quote: The deciduous trees (swamp white oaks) are arranged in rows and form informal clusters, clearings and groves. The park is at street level, above the Memorial Museum.

facts.fact: The victims' names are inscribed on 152 bronze parapets around the pools.
facts.quote: The names of 2,983 victims are inscribed on 152 bronze parapets on the memorial pools: 2,977 killed in the September 11 attacks and six killed in the 1993 World Trade Center bombing.

facts.fact: The memorial was dedicated on the tenth anniversary of the attacks, 11 September 2011, and opened to the public the next day.
facts.quote: A dedication ceremony commemorating the tenth anniversary of the attacks was held at the memorial on September 11, 2011, and it opened to the public the following day.

facts.fact: The Secretariat Building in Chandigarh was designed by Le Corbusier and completed in 1953 to house the offices of East Punjab's Chief Secretary.
facts.quote: Secretariat Building is a Le Corbusier-designed building in Chandigarh completed in 1953 to house the offices of the Chief Secretary of the Indian state of East Punjab.

facts.fact: Since Punjab was split in 1966, the building has been shared by the Chief Secretaries of Haryana and Punjab.
facts.quote: Since the Punjab Reorganisation Act, 1966 split East Punjab into Haryana and Punjab, Chandigarh has been the capital of both states and the Secretariat Building is shared by their respective Chief Secretaries.

facts.fact: It is one of three buildings and three monuments in the Chandigarh Capitol Complex, inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2016.
facts.quote: The Secretariat Building is one of three buildings and three monuments in the Chandigarh Capitol Complex, which is one of 17 sites dubbed "The Architectural Work of Le Corbusier" inscribed in July 2016 as a World Heritage Site by UNESCO.

facts.fact: Casa Batlló in central Barcelona is considered one of Gaudí's masterpieces; it is a remodel of an earlier house, redesigned by Gaudí in 1904.
facts.quote: It was designed by Antoni Gaudí, and is considered one of his masterpieces. A remodel of a previously built house, it was redesigned in 1904 by Gaudí (although the actual construction had not begun at this point) and has been refurbished several times since.

facts.fact: It stands on Passeig de Gràcia in the "Block of Discord", a row of strikingly different buildings by leading Modernista architects.
facts.quote: Casa Batlló is located on the Passeig de Gràcia in the Eixample district and forms part of a row of houses known as the Illa de la Discòrdia (or Mansana de la Discòrdia, the "Block of Discord"), so named because it features four striking, and strikingly different, buildings by noted Modernista architects of Barcelona.

facts.fact: There are few straight lines, and much of the facade is covered in trencadís, a mosaic of broken ceramic tiles.
facts.quote: There are few straight lines, and much of the façade is decorated with a colorful mosaic made of broken ceramic tiles (trencadís).

facts.fact: Gaudí enlarged the central well to bring light to the whole building and added new floors.
facts.quote: He expanded the central well in order to supply light to the whole building and also added new floors.

facts.fact: Locally it is called the House of Bones for its skeletal, biomorphic look.
facts.quote: The local name for the building is Casa dels ossos (House of Bones), as its biomorphic aesthetic has a skeletal quality.

facts.fact: The arched roof has been likened to the back of a dragon or dinosaur.
facts.quote: The roof is arched and was likened to the back of a dragon or dinosaur.

facts.fact: The loft has sixty catenary arches that read like an animal's ribcage.
facts.quote: It contains a series of sixty catenary arches that creates a space which represents the ribcage of an animal.

facts.fact: It became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2005.
facts.quote: In 2005, Casa Batlló became a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

facts.fact: The Royal Festival Hall is a 2,700-seat concert, dance and talks venue in the Southbank Centre on London's South Bank.
facts.quote: The Royal Festival Hall is a 2,700-seat concert, dance and talks venue within Southbank Centre in London, England.

facts.fact: In 1981 it became the first post-war building to be listed Grade I.
facts.quote: It is a Grade I listed building, the first post-war building to become so protected (in 1981).

facts.fact: It was built for the Festival of Britain for London County Council and opened on 3 May 1951.
facts.quote: The hall was built as part of the Festival of Britain for London County Council, and was officially opened on 3 May 1951.

facts.fact: The project was led by the LCC's chief architect Robert Matthew, with a young team including Leslie Martin, who came to lead it with Edwin Williams and Peter Moro.
facts.quote: The Festival Hall project was led by London County Council's then chief architect, Robert Matthew, who gathered around him a young team of talented designers including Leslie Martin, who was eventually to lead the project with Edwin Williams and Peter Moro, along with the furniture designer Robin Day and his wife, the textile designer Lucienne Day.

facts.fact: A 1948 sketch by Martin shows the concert hall as an "egg in a box".
facts.quote: A 1948 sketch by Martin shows the design of the concert hall as the egg in a box.

facts.fact: The wide open foyers were meant as meeting places for everyone, with no separate bars for different classes.
facts.quote: The wide open foyers, with bars and restaurants, were intended to be meeting places for all: there were to be no separate bars for different classes of patron.

facts.fact: It was built of reinforced concrete with fine woods and Derbyshire fossil limestone, and its exterior was bright white.
facts.quote: The hall they built used modernism's favourite material, reinforced concrete, alongside more luxurious elements including beautiful woods and Derbyshire fossilised limestone. The exterior of the building was bright white, intended to contrast with the blackened city surrounding it.

facts.fact: It was one of the first concert halls in the world designed using scientific acoustic principles.
facts.quote: The Festival Hall was one of the first concert halls in the world to be built using the application of scientific principles, both theoretical and experimental.

facts.fact: The Wotruba Church in Vienna was built from August 1974 to October 1976 to a design by Austrian sculptor Fritz Wotruba.
facts.quote: It was built between August 1974 and October 1976, based on a design by Austrian sculptor Fritz Wotruba.

facts.fact: Fritz Gerhard Mayr was the planning architect.
facts.quote: The building of the church was initiated by Margarethe Ottillinger, and designed by Wotruba. The planning architect was Fritz Gerhard Mayr.

facts.fact: Margarethe Ottillinger chose a former Nazi barracks site and wanted a bold religious and artistic statement in a secular age.
facts.quote: Ottillinger chose the site of former Nazi barracks, and wanted the new church to make a bold religious and artistic statement during a time of increasing secularization.

facts.fact: Wotruba died before it was finished, and Mayr oversaw the rest of the work.
facts.quote: Wotruba died before the completion of the church, and Mayr oversaw the remaining work.

facts.fact: Inspired by Chartres Cathedral, the Brutalist church is built of 152 concrete blocks with no visible symmetry, lit through clear glass windows.
facts.quote: Wotruba's church was inspired by Chartres Cathedral, and built in a Brutalist style. Built of 152 concrete blocks, it has no visible symmetry, and makes use of clear glass windows to provide light.

facts.fact: Wotruba's sculpture increasingly dissolved the figure into geometric abstraction based on the cube.
facts.quote: In his work, he increasingly dissolves figurative components in favor of geometrical abstraction with the shape of the cube as the basic form.

facts.fact: The Chapel of St. Ignatius is a Jesuit chapel on the Seattle University campus, completed in 1997.
facts.quote: The Chapel of St. Ignatius is a Jesuit chapel on the Seattle University campus in the U.S. state of Washington, completed in 1997.

facts.fact: It earned Steven Holl Architects the AIA Twenty-five Year Award, and a model of it is in the collection of MoMA in New York.
facts.quote: The design earned Steven Holl Architects a Twenty-five Year Award from the American Institute of Architects. A scale model of the building is in the permanent collection of the Museum of Modern Art in New York City.

facts.fact: Holl described it as "seven bottles of light in a stone box", with daylight coloured by painted baffles and coloured glass lenses.
facts.quote: Holl described his design for the chapel as "seven bottles of light in a stone box," with daylight taking on color by bouncing off colored baffles and passing through colored glass lenses.

facts.fact: At night the effect reverses, with coloured light glowing out of the building.
facts.quote: The same occurs in reverse at night, with light emanating from the building's internal illumination taking on color from the same mechanisms.

facts.fact: Each of the seven volumes of light stands for a different part of Jesuit Catholic worship.
facts.quote: Each volume represents a different part of Jesuit Catholic worship, and has differently colored glass so that various parts of the building are marked out by colored light.

facts.fact: Set in the middle of a former street, its long plan creates new campus quadrangles to the north, west and south.
facts.quote: The building is sited in the center of a former street and elongates the plan to create new campus quadrangles to the north, west and south, with a future quadrangle planned to the east.

facts.fact: Church on the Water is a privately owned wedding chapel in Tomamu, Hokkaido, Japan.
facts.quote: Church on the Water (Japanese: 水の教会) also known as Chapel on the Water is a privately owned wedding chapel in Tomamu, Shimukappu on the island of Hokkaido in Japan.

facts.fact: The chapel faces a large reflecting pool through a floor-to-ceiling window, in the Japanese tradition of shakkei (borrowed scenery).
facts.quote: The chapel faces a large reflecting pool visible through a large floor-to-ceiling window in the Japanese architectural tradition of shakkei.

facts.fact: Tadao Ando designed it in 1985.
facts.quote: The building is a notable project of Japanese modernist architect Tadao Ando who designed the structure in 1985.

facts.fact: Borobudur is the largest Buddhist temple in the world and one of the great archaeological sites of Southeast Asia.
facts.quote: Borobudur is the largest Buddhist temple in the world, and ranks with Bagan in Myanmar and Angkor Wat in Cambodia as one of the great archeological sites of Southeast Asia.

facts.fact: Built of grey andesite-like stone, it has nine stacked platforms, six square and three circular, topped by a central dome.
facts.quote: Constructed of gray andesite-like stone, the temple consists of nine stacked platforms, six square and three circular, topped by a central dome.

facts.fact: The central dome is ringed by 72 Buddha statues, each seated inside a perforated stupa.
facts.quote: The central dome is surrounded by 72 Buddha statues, each seated inside a perforated stupa.

facts.fact: Stairways and corridors lead pilgrims past 1,460 narrative relief panels.
facts.quote: The monument guides pilgrims through an extensive system of stairways and corridors with 1,460 narrative relief panels on the walls and the balustrades.

facts.fact: Built under the Sailendra dynasty, it follows Javanese Buddhist architecture, blending ancestor worship with the Buddhist idea of nirvana.
facts.quote: Built during the reign of the Sailendra dynasty, the temple design follows Javanese Buddhist architecture, which blends the Indonesian indigenous tradition of ancestor worship and the Buddhist concept of attaining nirvāṇa.

facts.fact: Seen from above, the single great stupa takes the form of a tantric Buddhist mandala on a square base about 118 metres a side.
facts.quote: Borobudur is built as a single large stupa and, when viewed from above, takes the form of a giant tantric Buddhist mandala, simultaneously representing the Buddhist cosmology and the nature of mind. The original foundation is a square, approximately 118 metres (387 ft) on each side.

facts.fact: During the restoration, over a million stones were taken down and individually identified, catalogued, cleaned and treated.
facts.quote: Over one million stones were dismantled and removed during the restoration, and set aside like pieces of a massive jig-saw puzzle to be individually identified, catalogued, cleaned and treated for preservation.

facts.fact: After the largest restoration, finished in 1983 with UNESCO, it was listed as a World Heritage Site.
facts.quote: The largest restoration project was completed in 1983 by the Indonesian government and UNESCO, followed by the monument's listing as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

facts.fact: Butaro Hospital is the district hospital for Burera District in Rwanda's Northern Province, about 96 km by road north of Kigali.
facts.quote: Butaro District Hospital is located in the Butaro Sector, of Burera District, in Rwanda's Northern Province, approximately 96 kilometres (60 mi), by road, north of Kigali, the national capital of Rwanda, and its largest city.

facts.fact: It was designed by MASS with Rwanda's Ministry of Health and Partners in Health.
facts.quote: The Butaro Hospital was designed by MASS in cooperation with the Rwandan Ministry of Health and Partners in Health.

facts.fact: Its design aims to fit the local environment and lower the risk of infections caught in hospital.
facts.quote: The facility features an innovative design intended to harmonize with the local environment and reduce the risk of hospital-acquired infections.

facts.fact: Construction of the 150-bed hospital began in December 2008, and it opened on 24 January 2011.
facts.quote: The construction of the 150-bed hospital begun in December 2008 and it was opened on 24 January 2011.

facts.fact: More than 3,500 local people worked on the building, finished a year ahead of schedule.
facts.quote: Construction was completed one year earlier than scheduled. Over 3,500 local community members were employed during construction.

facts.fact: Local materials were used wherever possible, including volcanic stone from the Virunga Mountains.
facts.quote: Wherever possible, the hospital was built using local materials, including volcanic stone from the Virunga Mountains.

facts.fact: The hospital now has 256 in-patient beds.
facts.quote: Butaro Hospital maintains 256 in-patient beds.

facts.fact: 56 Leonard Street, nicknamed the Jenga Building, is an 821-foot, 57-storey skyscraper in Tribeca, Manhattan.
facts.quote: 56 Leonard Street (known colloquially as the Jenga Building or Jenga Tower) is an 821 ft-tall (250 m), 57-story skyscraper on Leonard Street in the neighborhood of Tribeca in Manhattan, New York City.

facts.fact: Herzog & de Meuron designed it and describe it as "houses stacked in the sky"; it is the tallest structure in Tribeca.
facts.quote: Completed in 2017, the building was designed by the Swiss architecture firm Herzog & de Meuron, which describes the building as "houses stacked in the sky." It is the tallest structure in Tribeca.

facts.fact: Herzog & de Meuron also designed the interiors, including kitchens, bathrooms and fireplaces; Goldstein, Hill & West is the architect of record.
facts.quote: Herzog & de Meuron also designed the building's interiors, which include custom-designed kitchens, fixtures, bathrooms, and fireplaces. Goldstein, Hill & West Architects LLP is the architect of record.

facts.fact: Construction resumed in October 2012 after a pause of nearly four years.
facts.quote: After nearly four years, construction resumed in October 2012.

facts.fact: Eight full-floor apartments at the top have ceilings 14 to 19 feet high.
facts.quote: There are eight full-floor apartments at the top, ranging from 5,200 to 6,400 ft2 (480 to 590 m2), with 14-to-19 ft-high (4.3-to-5.8 m) ceilings.

facts.fact: An Anish Kapoor sculpture for its base, 19 feet tall and weighing 40 tons, was commissioned in 2008.
facts.quote: Measuring 19 feet in height, 48 feet in (curved) length, and weighing 40 tons, the sculpture was commissioned in 2008 at an estimated cost of $8–10 million.

facts.fact: In 2019 Curbed New York named it one of the city's 10 most important buildings of the decade.
facts.quote: 2019 Named as one of New York City’s 10 Most Important Buildings of the Past Decade, Curbed New York, a publication for American real estate and urban design.

facts.fact: Esplanade – Theatres on the Bay has two rounded structures: a concert hall of about 1,600 seats and a theatre of about 2,000.
facts.quote: Named after the nearby Esplanade Park, it consists of two rounded structures: one housing a concert hall with about 1,600 seats; and the other a theatre with a capacity of about 2,000 for the performing arts.

facts.fact: It was designed by DP Architects of Singapore with London's Michael Wilford & Partners, who left the project in 1995.
facts.quote: The building was designed by two architectural firms working in conjunction: by DP Architects (DPA) of Singapore and the London-based Michael Wilford & Partners (MWP), although the latter left the project in May 1995.

facts.fact: Two rounded space frames carry triangulated glass and sunshades, balancing outward views with shade from the sun.
facts.quote: The design consists of two rounded space frames fitted with triangulated glass elements and sunshades, which balance outward views with solar shading.

facts.fact: Critics said the first design, plain glass cases, would be a greenhouse in Singapore's tropical climate; aluminium sunshades were added to the final design.
facts.quote: Critics also accused that the design is insensitive to Singapore's location and climate as it would have created a greenhouse in the tropical climate of Singapore, but according to DPA director Vikas Gore some form of shading was always intended, and a cladding of aluminium sunshades was added to the final design.

facts.fact: More than 7,000 triangular aluminium sunshades cover its two glass shells, looking somewhat like the spikes of a durian.
facts.quote: More than 7,000 triangular aluminium sunshades that cover its two circular glass shell structures looked somewhat like spikes on two halves of the fruit.

facts.fact: The architects used glass for the views in every direction, but near the equator it also needed protection from heat and ultraviolet light.
facts.quote: They wanted to use glass because the views from Esplanade are beautiful in all directions, but since Singapore is so close to the equator, the structure also had to be protected from the Sun's heat and ultraviolet radiation.

facts.fact: The Lyric Theatre adapts the horseshoe form of a traditional European opera house.
facts.quote: The Lyric Theatre which has a capacity of about 2,000 seats is a type of an adaptation of the horseshoe form of a traditional European opera house.

facts.fact: Completed in February 2001, it opened officially on 12 October 2002.
facts.quote: Completed in February 2001, the centre was officially opened on 12 October 2002, by the then President of Singapore S. R. Nathan.

facts.fact: The Casa das Histórias Paula Rego is a museum in Cascais, Portugal, designed by Eduardo Souto de Moura to house works by the artist Paula Rego.
facts.quote: The Casa das Histórias Paula Rego ("House of Stories Paula Rego") is a museum in Cascais, Lisbon District, on the Portuguese Riviera, designed by the architect Eduardo Souto de Moura to house some of the works of the artist Paula Rego (1935 – 2022).

facts.fact: Chosen personally by Rego, Souto de Moura drew on the region's historic architecture, especially the nearby Palace of Sintra, in a contemporary way.
facts.quote: On the site of the disused tennis courts of the former Sporting Club of Cascais, the building designed by Souto De Moura, who was personally chosen by Paula Rego, uses the region's historical architecture, particularly the nearby Palace of Sintra, in a contemporary way.

facts.fact: Rego asked for a building that was "fun, lively and also a bit mischievous".
facts.quote: It was designed to be fully in keeping with her wishes, having indicated that it should be “fun, lively and also a bit mischievous”.

facts.fact: Its two pyramid-shaped towers and red concrete stand out, and the park's mature trees were kept as part of the design.
facts.quote: Its two pyramid-shaped towers and the red-coloured concrete are very distinctive and the previously existing mature trees of the park have been incorporated as elements in the design.

facts.fact: Four wings of different heights hold linked rooms around a central hall for temporary exhibitions.
facts.quote: The building consists of four wings, of different heights and sizes, subdivided into connecting rooms that are laid out around a central room designed to house temporary exhibitions.

facts.fact: It has 750 m² of exhibition space, a 200-seat auditorium, a shop and a café.
facts.quote: It has 750 m2 of exhibition space, together with a 200-seat auditorium, shop and café.

facts.fact: The museum was among the works cited when Souto de Moura won the 2011 Pritzker Prize.
facts.quote: The prize was awarded for his work including Estádio Municipal de Braga, the Burgo Tower in Porto and the Paula Rego Museum in Cascais.

facts.fact: Construction of the Alterlaa social housing complex began in the 1970s, with high-rises that step back on their lower floors.
facts.quote: In the 1970s, construction began on the Alterlaa social housing complex, featuring high-rises with distinctive setbacks on their lower floors.

facts.fact: Erlaa, in Vienna's Liesing district, is best known for this large residential complex, north of the old village centre.
facts.quote: To the west of Inzersdorf lies Erlaa, which is best known today for the large residential apartment complex, Wohnpark Alt-Erlaa, located north of the old centre of the village.

facts.fact: The Steilneset Memorial in Vardø, Norway, commemorates the 91 people tried and executed for witchcraft in 1621.
facts.quote: The monument commemorates the trial and execution in 1621 of 91 people for witchcraft.

facts.fact: It was designed by artist Louise Bourgeois and architect Peter Zumthor and opened in 2011; it was Bourgeois' last major work.
facts.quote: The memorial was designed by artist Louise Bourgeois and architect Peter Zumthor and was opened in 2011. It was Bourgeois' last major work.

facts.fact: It is linked to the development of Norway's National Tourist Routes.
facts.quote: The Steilneset Memorial was jointly commissioned by the town of Vardø, Finnmark County, the Varanger Museum, and the Norwegian Public Roads Administration, and has been associated with the development of the National Tourist Routes in Norway.

facts.fact: It has two buildings: a 120-metre wooden structure framing a fabric cocoon for Zumthor's installation, and a square smoked-glass room for Bourgeois' work.
facts.quote: The Memorial comprises two separate buildings: a 410-foot (120 m) long wooden structure framing a fabric cocoon that contains Zumthor's installation; and a square smoked glass room, its roof 39 feet (12 m) on each side, that contains the work of Bourgeois.

facts.fact: Zumthor's structure is made of wooden frames built off-site and assembled into sixty bays, with a fibreglass membrane hung inside on cable-stays.
facts.quote: Zumthor's structure is made from wooden frames, fabricated off-site and assembled to create sixty bays in a long line within which, suspended by cable-stays, is a coated fibreglass membrane that tapers at each end.

facts.fact: Inside, a 100-metre timber walkway only 1.5 metres wide passes 91 small windows, one for each person executed, each with a text based on original sources.
facts.quote: Inside is a timber walkway, 328 feet (100 m) long but just 5 feet (1.5 m) wide, and along the narrow corridor are 91 randomly placed small windows representing those executed, each one accompanied by an explanatory text based on original sources.

facts.fact: Bourgeois' pavilion is built of weathering steel and 17 panes of tinted glass, with walls that stop short of floor and ceiling.
facts.quote: Its square structure is fabricated from weathering steel and 17 panes of tinted glass, forming walls that stop short of the ceiling and floor.

facts.fact: The Bridge of Peace is a bow-shaped steel and glass footbridge over the Kura River, linking Rike Park with the Old Town in central Tbilisi.
facts.quote: The Bridge of Peace (Georgian: მშვიდობის ხიდი, mshvidobis khidi) is a bow-shaped pedestrian bridge, a steel and glass construction illuminated with numerous LEDs, over the Kura River, linking the Rike Park with Old town in central Tbilisi.

facts.fact: The 150-metre bridge was ordered by Tbilisi City Hall as a contemporary link between the old town and the new district, and opened on 6 May 2010.
facts.quote: The bridge, which stretches 150 metres (490 ft) over the Kura River, was ordered by the City Hall of Tbilisi to create a contemporary design feature connecting Old Tbilisi with the new district. The official opening took place on May 6, 2010.

facts.fact: It was designed by Italian architect Michele De Lucchi, with lighting by French designer Philippe Martinaud.
facts.quote: The bridge was designed by the Italian architect Michele De Lucchi, who had also designed the buildings of the Ceremonial Palace of Georgia and the Ministry of Internal Affairs in Tbilisi; the lighting design was created by the French lighting designer Philippe Martinaud.

facts.fact: The structure was built in Italy and brought to Tbilisi in 200 trucks.
facts.quote: The structure of the bridge was built in Italy and transported to Tbilisi in 200 trucks, while the lighting was installed on site during the assembly of the structures.

facts.fact: Its curving steel and glass canopy, likened to a sea creature, is lit at night by thousands of white LEDs.
facts.quote: The bridge, a design of which reminds one of a marine animal, has a curvy steel and glass canopy top which shimmers with an interactive light display at night, generated by thousands of white LEDs.

facts.fact: 240 motion sensors light the LEDs in the glass railings as people walk across.
facts.quote: Within the bridge walkway, the low-power linear LED arrays embedded in the glass railings are triggered by 240 motion sensors as the pedestrians pass, giving an impression that the bridge lights come on for each person setting foot on the bridge.

facts.fact: Critics said the bridge dominated the historic old town and hid its landmarks.
facts.quote: Several opposition politicians, architects, and urban planners unleashed criticism, complaining that the bridge unduly dominated the historical old town and obscured the area's old architectural landmarks.

facts.fact: The London Eye, first called the Millennium Wheel, is the world's tallest cantilevered observation wheel, on the South Bank of the Thames.
facts.quote: The London Eye, originally the Millennium Wheel, is a cantilevered observation wheel on the South Bank of the River Thames in London. It is the world's tallest cantilevered observation wheel, and the most popular paid tourist attraction in the United Kingdom with more than three million visitors annually.

facts.fact: Unlike taller wheels, it is cantilevered, supported only by an A-frame on one side.
facts.quote: Unlike taller wheels, the Eye is cantilevered and supported solely by an A-frame on one side.

facts.fact: It was conceived by architects David Marks and Julia Barfield, a husband-and-wife team.
facts.quote: The London Eye was conceived by architects David Marks and Julia Barfield, a husband-and-wife team who met in 1972 while studying at the Architectural Association and living in squats in Stockwell, south London.

facts.fact: They saw a wheel as a way to lift people up high easily while avoiding comparison with the Eiffel Tower.
facts.quote: The pair realised that a wheel could “get people up high easily, efficiently and effortlessly” while avoiding comparisons with the Eiffel Tower.

facts.fact: The rim is held by tensioned steel cables, like a giant spoked bicycle wheel.
facts.quote: The rim of the Eye is supported by tensioned steel cables and resembles a huge spoked bicycle wheel.

facts.fact: It was built in sections floated up the Thames, assembled flat in the river, then lifted upright.
facts.quote: The wheel was constructed in sections which were floated up the Thames on barges and assembled lying flat on piled platforms in the river.

facts.fact: The wheel turns at 26 cm per second, so one revolution takes about 30 minutes.
facts.quote: The wheel rotates at 26 cm (10 in) per second (about 0.9 km/h or 0.6 mph) so that one revolution takes about 30 minutes, giving a theoretical capacity of 1,600 passengers per hour.

facts.fact: Planned as a temporary attraction on a five-year lease, it was given permanent status in 2002.
facts.quote: The London Eye was originally intended as a temporary attraction, with a five-year lease. In December 2001, operators submitted an application to Lambeth Council to give the London Eye permanent status, and the application was granted in July 2002.

facts.fact: The Basilica of the Annunciation is a Catholic church in Nazareth, built over what Catholic tradition holds to be the site of the house of the Virgin Mary.
facts.quote: It was established over what Catholic tradition holds to be the site of the house of the Virgin Mary.

facts.fact: The new basilica, designed by Italian architect Giovanni Muzio, was built by Solel Boneh from 1960 to 1969.
facts.quote: The new basilica was designed by the Italian architect Giovanni Muzio, and built by the Israeli building firm Solel Boneh during the years 1960–1969.

facts.fact: Its style is sometimes described as Italian Brutalism.
facts.quote: It is built in a style sometimes characterised as Italian Brutalism.

facts.fact: It is a two-storey building finished in 1969 over the sites of earlier Byzantine and Crusader churches.
facts.quote: The current Catholic Church is a two-storey building finished in 1969 over the site of earlier churches from the Byzantine, Crusader, and the Israeli -period churches.

facts.fact: The lower level holds the Grotto of the Annunciation, believed by many Christians to be the remains of Mary's childhood home.
facts.quote: The lower level contains the Grotto of the Annunciation, believed by many Christians to be the remains of the original childhood home of Mary.

facts.fact: The upper level holds images of Mary, mostly mosaics, each from a different country with a large Catholic population.
facts.quote: The upper level contains a number of images of Mary, mainly mosaics, each from a different country with significant Catholic population.

facts.fact: It is the largest church building in the Middle East under the Congregation for the Oriental Churches, and remains under Franciscan control.
facts.quote: Used by the Latin parish, it remains under the control of the Franciscans. It is the largest Christian Church building or sanctuary in the Middle East under the supervision of the Congregation for the Oriental Churches.

facts.fact: The Hungarian Parliament Building in Budapest is the seat of Hungary's National Assembly.
facts.quote: The Hungarian Parliament Building (Hungarian: Országház [ˈorsaːkhaːz], lit. 'House of the Country'), also known as the Parliament of Budapest after its location, is the seat of the National Assembly of Hungary, a notable landmark of Hungary, and a popular tourist destination in Budapest.

facts.fact: Imre Steindl designed it in neo-Gothic style; it opened in 1902 and has been Hungary's largest building ever since.
facts.quote: It was designed by Hungarian architect Imre Steindl in neo-Gothic style and opened in 1902. It has been the largest building in Hungary since its completion.

facts.fact: Steindl won an international competition, partly because his plans resembled the Palace of Westminster in London.
facts.quote: One reason that Steindl's proposal was chosen is that his neo-Gothic plans bore a strong resemblance with the Palace of Westminster in London.

facts.fact: Construction began in 1885, and the building was inaugurated in 1896, the presumed 1,000th anniversary of the country.
facts.quote: Construction from the winning plan was started in 1885, and the building was inaugurated on the presumed 1,000th anniversary of the country in 1896.

facts.fact: The Gothic Revival building has a symmetrical facade and a Renaissance Revival central dome, with two identical parliament halls on opposite sides.
facts.quote: The Parliament Building is built in the Gothic Revival style; it has a symmetrical façade and a central dome. The dome is Renaissance Revival architecture. The parliament is also largely symmetrical from the inside, with two identical parliament halls on the opposing sides of the building.

facts.fact: It is 268 metres long and 123 metres wide, with 691 rooms and 10 courtyards.
facts.quote: It is 268 m (879 ft) long and 123 m (404 ft) wide, making it the largest building in the country since its construction. Its interior includes 10 courtyards, 13 passenger and freight elevators, 27 gates, 29 staircases and 691 rooms (which includes more than 200 offices).

facts.fact: Its 96-metre height refers to the founding of the Hungarian principality in 896.
facts.quote: Its height of 96 m (315 ft) is an allusion to the purported nation's millennium in 1896, with the establishment of the Principality of Hungary in 896 following the Hungarian conquest of the Carpathian Basin.

facts.fact: The sixteen-sided central hall has held the Holy Crown of Hungary since 2000.
facts.quote: The Holy Crown of Hungary, which is also depicted in Hungary's coat of arms, has been displayed in the central hall since 2000.

facts.fact: The Australian War Memorial in Canberra is a national memorial, museum and archive for all Australians who have died as a result of war.
facts.quote: The Australian War Memorial (AWM) is a national war memorial, museum and archive dedicated to all Australians who have died as a result of war, including peacekeeping duties.

facts.fact: After a 1925–26 design competition produced no winner, Emil Sodersten and John Crust were asked to combine Sodersten's Art Deco style with Crust's cost-cutting approach.
facts.quote: Instead Emil Sodersten and John Crust were asked to collaborate and create a design that incorporates Sodersten's Art Deco style with Crust's cost-cutting approach.

facts.fact: The Great Depression delayed construction; the Memorial opened to the public in 1941.
facts.quote: Designs for the AWM were created by Emil Sodersten and John Crust, although the onset of the Great Depression delayed its construction. Work on the Memorial Building progressed in the mid-1930s, and the AWM was officially opened to the public in 1941.

facts.fact: The Memorial Building is Art Deco, with Byzantine and Egyptian motifs in its interlocking masses and the pylons at its front.
facts.quote: The building was designed in an Art Deco style, with Byzantine and Egyptian motifs in its interpenetrating masses and pylons at its front.

facts.fact: It sits at the end of the land axis of Walter Burley Griffin's plan for Canberra, with a clear line of sight to Parliament House.
facts.quote: The AWM's positioning along this axis was deliberate to reflect its national importance and provide it with a clear line of sight to Parliament House and vice versa.

facts.fact: The courtyard holds a reflecting pool, with steps at its north end up to the Hall of Memory.
facts.quote: The courtyard contains a reflecting pool and steps up its northern end leading to the Hall of Memory.

facts.fact: Napier Waller's mosaics in the Hall of Memory were installed in 1955; his murals are the largest in Australia.
facts.quote: Ewers's final design, Australian Serviceman was accepted in 1955, the same year Waller's mosaics were installed in the Memorial Building's Hall of Memory. Waller's murals are the largest installed in Australia.

facts.fact: The Tomb of the Unknown Australian Soldier was placed in the Hall of Memory in 1993.
facts.quote: In 1993, the Tomb of the Unknown Australian Soldier was installed inside the Memorial Building's Hall of Memory.

facts.fact: The Napier Museum is an art and natural history museum in Thiruvananthapuram, India.
facts.quote: The Napier Museum is an art and natural history museum situated in Thiruvananthapuram, India.

facts.fact: It was completed and opened in 1880, named after the Governor of Madras, Francis Napier.
facts.quote: In 1880, construction finished and the museum opened to the public, bearing the namesake of its governor, Francis Napier, 10th Lord Napier.

facts.fact: The Indo-Saracenic building has no air conditioning but has always relied on good natural ventilation.
facts.quote: The Indo-Saracenic structure lacks an air conditioning system. Although it has never been an issue due to suitable natural ventilation, an annex built in 2016 was noted for various problems such as mold, insects and corrosion owing to the lack of windows and openings.

facts.fact: Its features include a Gothic roof and minarets.
facts.quote: Some of the building features include a gothic roof and minarets.

facts.fact: Its ornament and style draw on Indian, Chinese, Kerala and Mughal architecture.
facts.quote: The Napier Museum, a landmark of the city, is noted for its unique ornamentation and architectural style, which is influenced by Indian, Chinese, Kerala and Mughal schools of architecture.

facts.fact: The museum has a bandstand with concealed speakers and special acoustics.
facts.quote: The museum has a bandstand with concealed speakers and special acoustics.

facts.fact: Its architect, Robert Chisholm, was a British architect who pioneered the Indo-Saracenic style in Madras.
facts.quote: Robert Fellowes Chisholm (11 January 1840 – 28 May 1915) was a British architect who pioneered the Indo-Saracenic style of architecture in Madras.

facts.fact: The Gehry Residence was Frank Gehry's own home, first built as an extension around an existing Dutch colonial style house.
facts.quote: The Gehry Residence is the former home of architect Frank Gehry. It was originally an extension, designed by Gehry and built around an existing Dutch colonial style house.

facts.fact: It uses unconventional materials such as chain-link fencing and corrugated steel.
facts.quote: It makes use of unconventional materials, such as chain-link fences and corrugated steel.

facts.fact: It is sometimes considered one of the earliest deconstructivist buildings, though Gehry denied this.
facts.quote: It is sometimes considered one of the earliest deconstructivist buildings, although Gehry denied this.

facts.fact: In 1977 Frank and Berta Gehry bought a pink bungalow built in 1920.
facts.quote: In 1977, Frank and Berta Gehry bought a pink bungalow originally built in 1920.

facts.fact: In 1978 he wrapped the house in a new exterior while leaving the old one visible.
facts.quote: In 1978, he chose to wrap the house with a new exterior while leaving the old exterior visible.

facts.fact: He barely touched the rear and south facades and added tilted glass cubes on the other sides.
facts.quote: He hardly touched the rear and south facades, and to the other sides of the house he added tilted glass cubes.

facts.fact: Many neighbours were unhappy with the unusual architecture.
facts.quote: Many of Gehry's neighbors were unhappy with the unusual architecture appearing in their neighborhood.

facts.fact: Casa Calvet was designed by Gaudí for a textile manufacturer, combining commercial space in the basement and ground floor with a residence.
facts.quote: Casa Calvet (Catalan pronunciation: [ˈkazə kəlˈβɛt]) is a building, designed by Antoni Gaudí for a textile manufacturer which served as both a commercial property (in the basement and on the ground floor) and a residence.

facts.fact: It stands at Carrer de Casp 48 in Barcelona's Eixample and was built between 1898 and 1900.
facts.quote: It is located at Carrer de Casp 48, Eixample district of Barcelona. It was built between 1898 and 1900.

facts.fact: Scholars agree it is Gaudí's most conventional work, partly because it had to fit between older buildings in an elegant part of the city.
facts.quote: Gaudí scholars agree that this building is the most conventional of his works, partly because it had to be squeezed in between older structures and partly because it was sited in one of the most elegant sections of Barcelona.

facts.fact: Its symmetry and orderly rhythm are unusual for Gaudí, though the curved double gable and the projecting oriel over the entrance are modernista touches.
facts.quote: Its symmetry, balance and orderly rhythm are unusual for Gaudí's works. However, the curves and double gable at the top, the projecting oriel at the entrance — almost baroque in its drama, and isolated witty details are modernista elements.

facts.fact: Bulging balconies alternate with smaller, shallower ones.
facts.quote: Bulging balconies alternate with smaller, shallower balconies.

facts.fact: The columns beside the entrance are shaped like stacked bobbins, a nod to the family's textile business.
facts.quote: Columns flanking the entrance are in the form of stacked bobbins — an allusion to the family business of textile manufacture.

facts.fact: The ground-floor gallery combines wrought iron and stone.
facts.quote: Lluís Permanyer claims that "the gallery at ground level is the façade's most outstanding feature, a daring combination of wrought iron and stone in which decorative historical elements such as a cypress, an olive tree, horns of plenty, and the Catalan coat of arms can be discerned".

facts.fact: Casa Calvet was among the modernist buildings recognised by the Arts Building Annual Award, given between 1899 and 1906.
facts.quote: Between 1899 and 1906, the Arts Building Annual Award (Concurso annual de edificios artísticos) awarded  modernist pieces, like the Casa Calvet, the Casa Lleó Morera and the Casa Trinxet.

facts.fact: Dresden Hauptbahnhof is the largest passenger station in Dresden; it replaced the Bohemian station in 1898.
facts.quote: Dresden Hauptbahnhof ("main station", abbreviated Dresden Hbf) is the largest passenger station in the Saxon capital of Dresden. In 1898, it replaced the Böhmischen Bahnhof ("Bohemian station") of the former Saxon-Bohemian State Railway (Sächsisch-Böhmische Staatseisenbahn), and was designed with its formal layout as the central station of the city.

facts.fact: Its combination of a station building on an island between the tracks and a terminal on two levels is unique.
facts.quote: The combination of a station building on an island between the tracks and a terminal station on two different levels is unique.

facts.fact: The design came from an 1892 competition; Dresden architects Ernst Giese and Paul Weidner shared first prize and led construction.
facts.quote: Dresden architects Ernst Giese and Paul Weidner and Leipzig architect Arwed Roßbach each won a first prize. The realised design incorporates elements of both drafts. Construction began in the same year, led by Ernst Giese and Paul Weidner.

facts.fact: The platform halls used 17,000 tonnes of steel, and the masonry is Elbe Sandstone.
